narr: Tropical moisture surged northwards as a developing area of low pressure (PTC #8) off the coast of the Carolinas began to move inland. Heavy tropical rains associated with the low began on the 16th and continued on the 17th across the Outer Banks.
ev: NWS employee reports multiple feet of water on Neptune Drive in Cape Carteret.
Duplin County 911 Center reported multiple flooded roads.
Public report of impassable roads due to high water at the intersection of Sound Drive and Miller Drive in Emerald Isle.
The Reed Road closed due to high water.
Road under water and reports of flooding by Lowes Hardware and Family Tire in Morehead City.
NWS Employee observed water several inches deep flowing across Nine Mile Road.
The public reported that the intersection of Campen Road and Carraway Drive was under water.
The public reported that Beaufort Manor Drive was under water.
Public reported that Russell Creek Road near the entrance to Deerfield Shores was under water.
Public reported that Firetown Road in Otway was flooded.
Public reported that Community Road in Davis was flooded.
Public reported that the intersection of Merrimon and Laurel Road was impassable.
Public reported that Tuttles Grove Road was flooded.
Dare County dispatch reported several roads flooded in Duck, Southern Shores, and Kill Devil Hills. Travel in some areas was difficult to impossible. Water was nearly a foot deep in spots.
The mPING report of flooded roads in Kitty Hawk.
NC DOT webcams show flooding ongoing along NC 12 through Duck, including around the intersections of NC 12 and Hillcrest and NC 12 and Dogwood. Flooding extends into nearby sidewalks and yards.
Multiple reports of flooded roads from Duck to Southern Shores.
